#LD clumping

```{r}
show_loci(madagascar)$chromosome <- as.integer(show_loci(madagascar)$chromosome)

show_loci(madagascar) <- madagascar %>% show_loci() %>% arrange(chr_int,position)

madagascar <- gt_impute_simple(madagascar, method = "random")

to_keep_LD <- loci_ld_clump(madagascar, thr_r2 = 0.5, size = 50, return_id = TRUE)
#Previous Error: Not compatible with requested type: [type=character; target=double].

#Error: 'infos.chr' should contain only integers.

madagascar <- madagascar%>% select_loci(all_of(to_keep_LD))

```

```{r}
#Read in Pierron Malagasy metadata

pop_table <- read.table(resrepo::path_resrepo("data/raw/data_input/Madagascar_Borneo.poptable"), sep = "\t", fill = TRUE)
colnames(pop_table) <- c("IID", "V2","FID","Population","V5","V6","V7")

#Remove the "RR"
madagascar$id <- sub("RR.*", "", madagascar$id)

#Find Malagasy entries 
pop_table_sub <- subset(pop_table,pop_table$IID %in% madagascar$id & pop_table$V5 =="Madagascar")

#match up the ID's with pop table metadata
matching_m <- match(madagascar$id, pop_table_sub$IID)

madagascar$population <- ifelse(!is.na(matching_m), pop_table_sub$Population[matching_m], madagascar$population)

```

```{r}
madagascar <- madagascar %>% group_by(population)
runs <- gt_roh_window(madagascar,
                            window_size = 15,
                            threshold = 0.05,
                            min_snp = 3,
                            heterozygosity = FALSE,
                            max_opp_window = 1,
                            max_miss_window = 1,
                            max_gap = 10^6,
                            min_length_bps = 1000,
                            min_density = 0.1)
```


# Total number of runs

```{r}
runs_per_indiv <- runs %>% group_by(id) %>% count()

madagascar <- left_join(madagascar, runs_per_indiv, by = "id")
#madagascar$n <- as.factor(madagascar$n)
madagascar$n <- as.numeric(madagascar$n)
madagascar$population <- as.factor(madagascar$population)
```

```{r}
ggplot(data=madagascar, aes(x=id , y=n, fill=population)) +
  geom_bar(stat="identity") + 
  coord_flip()+
  theme(axis.text.x = element_blank(), axis.ticks.x = element_blank(), axis.text.y = element_blank(), axis.ticks.y = element_blank())+
  labs(x = "Number of runs", y = "ID", fill = "Population")
```


```{r}
ggplot(madagascar,aes(x=population, y = n, fill = population))+
geom_violin()+
labs(title = "Number of runs of homozygosity per individual", y = "Number", x = NULL, fill = "Population")
```

# Total length of runs

```{r}
total_length_per_indiv <- aggregate(runs$lengthBps, by = list(id = runs$id), FUN = sum)
colnames(total_length_per_indiv) <- c("id","length")
madagascar <- left_join(madagascar, total_length_per_indiv, by = "id")
```

```{r}
ggplot(data=madagascar, aes(x=id , y=length, fill=population)) +
  geom_bar(stat="identity") + 
  coord_flip()+
  theme(axis.text.x = element_blank(), axis.ticks.x = element_blank(), axis.text.y = element_blank(), axis.ticks.y = element_blank())+
  labs(x = "Total length", y = "ID", fill = "Population")
```


```{r}
ggplot(madagascar,aes(x=population, y = length, fill = population))+
geom_violin()+
labs(title = "Total length of runs of homozygosity per individual", y = "Length (BPs)", x = NULL, fill = "Population")
```


# Average length of runs per individual

```{r}
avg_length_per_indiv <- aggregate(runs$lengthBps, by = list(id = runs$id), FUN = mean)
colnames(avg_length_per_indiv) <- c("id","mean")
madagascar <- left_join(madagascar, avg_length_per_indiv, by = "id")
```

```{r}
ggplot(data=madagascar, aes(x=id , y=mean, fill=population)) +

  theme(axis.text.x = element_blank(), axis.ticks.x = element_blank(), axis.text.y = element_blank(), axis.ticks.y = element_blank())+

```


```{r}
ggplot(madagascar,aes(x=population, y = mean, fill = population))+
geom_violin()+
labs(title = "Mean length of runs of homozygosity per individual", y = "Length (BPs)", x = NULL, fill = "Population")
```

We could test using Kruskal-wallis whether there is a significant diff between 
groups in both number and total length of ROH's. But, this may not answer our 
question. 

We may expect to see higher ROH's in individuals with more Asian ancestry among
the Merina, but we have several confounding effects:

1) Merina with higher African ancestry will be likely to have fewer ROH's anyway, 
as African popualtions have lower homozygosity than other global pops

2) IBD analysis (Alva et al 2022) suggests a bottleneck in the Asian ancestry 
source of all Malagasy people, meaning (if all other things were equal) the Asian 
ancestry component would have more ROH's than the African component 


Ideas:

Anything else we can use as a proxy for caste? Not really, the groups live side by 
side, so location won't help.

Correlations of ROH versus ancestry for all individuals, regardless of ethnic group
Correlations of ROH versus ethnicity for all individuals, regardless of ancestry

Analyse, see how well each explains the data

A model including the effects of both should be the best fit?


Could we remove the Merina, predict based on the correlation of ancestry/ROH's in the
other data where they should fall in ROH distribution given their ancestry, and 
then show that that model alone doesn't account for the inflation in ROH's?
